title: Diagnosis at the correct layer
task_statement: Name the faulty layer with evidence before you change a prompt, model, or tool. (Inference: wording from secondary sources)

components.name: Cache miss diagnosis
components.first_principle: The earliest divergence in a request explains the miss, so find that divergence before any other fix.
steps: Include the diagnostics object on every turn of the conversation.
Set diagnostics.previous_message_id to the id of the previous response.
Read cache_miss_reason in the response when the cache read count drops.
Match the reason type to the layer that changed: model, system, tools, or messages.
Fix the earliest divergence first, because later reasons can hide behind it.
Confirm the fix with the cache read token count on the next request.
pros: The response names the type of change that broke the cached prefix.
The four changed types estimate the input tokens after the divergence point.
Diagnostics do not block or fail the request.
cons: Diagnostics are available on the Claude API only.
Fingerprints expire after a short period, so compare close requests.
A comparison works only within the same organization and workspace.
use_when: The cache hit rate drops after a prompt or tool change.
Cache read tokens stay at zero for a prefix that repeats.
A team must find which layer changed the cached prefix.
do_not_use_when: The workload runs on Amazon Bedrock or Claude Models on Google Cloud (Google managed).
The cause sits outside the request, such as a provider update. (Inference)
The team needs only a total cost figure, which the usage fields already give.

constraints.choice: Include the diagnostics object on every turn.
constraints.combination: Log cache_miss_reason next to the usage fields.

constraints.choice: Fix a cache miss before you change the cache duration. (Inference)
constraints.combination: Compare the 5-minute and 1-hour write prices after the fix.

constraints.choice: Restore the cached prefix so that requests read cached tokens. (Inference)
Compare requests only within the same organization and workspace.
Rely on fingerprints that hold hashes and token counts, not prompt text.

components.exam_tie: D4.4. Expect a scenario where cache reads drop after an edit, and an option proposes a bigger model. The credited answer finds the changed block first. (Inference)
components.trap: A bigger model tier to recover a lower hit rate. The tier change adds cost, and the prefix still changes on every request.
components.decision_rule: Find the earliest changed block in the prefix, and move the variable content after the breakpoint.
components.exam_tip: Zero cache read and zero cache write counts point to a prompt below the minimum cacheable length, not to a model choice.

components.name: Grounding and consistency checks
components.first_principle: An unsupported claim is easier to catch when the answer must point to its source text.

nodes.label: Extra samples of the same prompt
Accept, flag, or I do not know

steps: Give Claude explicit permission to say that it does not know.
Ask Claude to extract word-for-word quotes before the main task on long documents.
Ask Claude to cite a quote for each claim, and to retract a claim that has no quote.
Run the same prompt several times and compare the answers for inconsistencies.
Review the summarized thinking when an answer looks wrong.
Ask Claude to verify each earlier claim in a follow-up prompt.
pros: Citations give a reviewer a check that needs no second model call. (Inference)
The docs say inconsistencies across outputs could indicate hallucinations.
The docs say the I do not know option can drastically reduce false information.
cons: Several runs multiply cost and latency. (Inference)
Summarized thinking shows a summary, not every reasoning step. (Inference)
Quote extraction adds tokens before the main task. (Inference)
use_when: Answers cite facts or figures that users rely on.
Answers vary across runs for the same question.
The source document is long and the answer must match it.
do_not_use_when: The latency limit leaves no room for extra calls. (Inference)
The task is creative and has no source text to check against. (Inference)

constraints.choice: Run extra samples only for answers that need a check. (Inference)
constraints.combination: Stream the first answer so that users see text early. (Inference)

constraints.choice: Fix the number of samples for each check. (Inference)
constraints.combination: Cache the shared source prefix across samples. (Inference)

constraints.choice: Track the disagreement rate between samples for each task type. (Inference)
Keep flagged answers and their quotes for audit. (Inference)
Use retrieval to ground answers in the right source passages.

components.exam_tie: D4.4. Expect a scenario with a plausible but unsupported answer and a request for more capacity. The credited answer adds grounding checks before any capacity change. (Inference)
components.trap: A stronger model added to fix invented facts. The model can still invent facts without a check that ties each claim to a source.
components.decision_rule: Require a quote or citation for each claim, and allow the model to say that it does not know.
components.exam_tip: Answers that change across runs for the same input signal a possible hallucination that a check can catch.

decision_flow:
flowchart TD
  A{Quality dropped after a change?} -->|No| X[Keep monitoring]
  A -->|Yes| B{Cache reads dropped?}
  B -->|Yes| C[Read cache miss reason]
  C --> D[Fix the earliest divergence]
  B -->|No| E{Answer has a checkable source?}
  E -->|Yes| F[Require quotes and citations]
  E -->|No| G[Run samples and compare them]
cheatsheet:
flowchart LR
  S[Symptom] --> E[Evidence per layer]
  E --> H[Hypotheses]
  H --> T[Split test]
  T --> F[Smallest fix]
  F --> R[Regression check]
  E --> C[cache_miss_reason]
  E --> Q[Quotes and citations]

patterns.rule: Ask for quotes first, then require a citation for each claim.
traps: Add tools without a grounding step

patterns.wording: quality drops after a prompt edit while the model stays the same
patterns.answer_type: layer-by-layer diagnosis with a split test
patterns.rule: Name the changed layer first, then test the suspects one at a time.

patterns.wording: cache reads fall to zero after a template edit
patterns.rule: Read cache_miss_reason, fix the earliest divergence, and confirm with cache read counts.
